title: Types of Insurance Regulated by IRDAI

blocks.content: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) is a statutory body tasked with regulating and promoting the insurance and re-insurance industries in India.

rows: Must exist at the time of purchase
Must exist at the time of claim/loss

items: Life Insurance contracts are contracts of assurance, while General Insurance contracts are strictly contracts of indemnity.
IRDAI was established based on the recommendations of the Malhotra Committee report of 1994.
Insurable interest must exist at the time of loss in General Insurance (except Marine Cargo), but only at the inception of policy in Life Insurance.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: IRDAI classifies insurance broadly into two primary sectors: Life Insurance and General (Non-Life) Insurance.
Life Insurance acts as a contract of assurance, offering financial protection against the risk of human life loss.
General Insurance operates on the principle of indemnity and covers property, health, motor, marine, and travel risks.
Health Insurance is regulated separately but offered by both general insurance companies and Standalone Health Insurers (SAHI).
Reinsurance involves insuring the insurance companies themselves to manage large capital risks and solvency.
